reasoning: Minnesota has leaned Democratic in recent elections. Tim Walz (D) won the governorship in 2018 and 2022. However, Walz became VP candidate in 2024, so he likely won't run in 2026. The Democratic nominee would be a new candidate. Minnesota's partisan lean is D+3-4. Without an incumbent advantage, the race becomes more competitive. Historical patterns show Minnesota gubernatorial races can be close. Given Democratic structural advantages in Minnesota but uncertainty around the nominee and national political environment in 2026, I estimate moderate Democratic advantage.
